cohort: 4,244 mothers in Pelotas, Southern Brazil, who gave birth in 2004
finding: Cesarean sections were associated with a higher risk of early maternal complications, including postpartum infection, urinary tract infection, pain, headaches, and anesthetic complications, but not with late complications.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with a 56% higher risk of early complications, 2.98 times higher risk of postpartum infection, 79% higher risk of urinary tract infection, 2.40 times higher risk of pain, 6.16 times higher risk of headaches, and 12 times higher risk of anesthetic complications compared to vaginal delivery.
